title: Codex Mendoza
shelf_note: A colonial Mexican pictorial manuscript with Nahuatl glosses in Spanish hand. Its date (1541) is plausible. Calling the language "Nahuatl" undersells it, because the codex's commentary is Spanish and its main content is pictographic.
structure_note: The structure block says pages_translated is 0, but pages_translated_field says 140, so one of these instruments is wrong (E2). Only 96 of 188 records have a printed number, with 16 backsteps and 26 repeats. This leaf carries two numbering systems: "7" at the top centre and "11/2" at the top right. Mixed foliation schemes and blank versos most likely explain the backsteps and repeats, not a splice. The count of 151 pages with OCR against 188 records fits the many blank leaves. The worse problem is that blank leaves like this one were OCR'd from the neighbouring page's strip.

pages.layout: blank verso showing faint text and a circular figure drawing through from the other side; a strip of the facing leaf at the left edge holds conquest (burning-temple) glyphs with glosses; a ruler at the right

ocr_errors.image: the leaf itself is blank except for "7" and "11/2"; the only ink is show-through
ocr_errors.problem: a blank verso is tagged as a text page

ocr_errors.image: "tepeyacac" and the other five glosses sit only in the strip of the FACING leaf at the left edge of the frame
ocr_errors.problem: the whole transcription comes from the neighbouring leaf's edge strip, not from this leaf, so none of it is this page's text

ocr_errors.ocr: Each consisting of a stylized hill (tepetl) with a specific iconographic element on top
ocr_errors.image: the visible glyphs are tilted temples with flames and smoke scrolls on stepped platforms (the conquest sign); the hill place-signs are cut off at the left, and a reclining human figure above the last glyph is not mentioned
ocr_errors.problem: the image description misidentifies what is visible
"tecalco" misread as "tecaloo", and the pueblo abbreviation "pu°" misread as ".pi" (also in "havlom.pi")

ocr_errors.image: the gloss is partly cut at the gutter; it probably reads "ocuilan"
ocr_errors.problem: a probable u→n and a→o misreading; low confidence at this resolution

tr_errors.english: This page shows a column of six Aztec place-glyphs, each a hill sign topped with a symbol that spells a town name
tr_errors.problem: a blank leaf is presented as carrying six place-glyphs and a list of towns; the content belongs to the facing leaf, so it is not a translation of this page

tr_errors.english: This page continues the list of conquered towns from the previous page.
tr_errors.problem: a continuity claim for a blank verso; the town list is the previous page itself, seen at the edge of the frame

tr_errors.english: The gloss probably corresponds to Ocuilan, listed on the previous page.
tr_errors.problem: asserts what the previous page lists, which this record does not carry

tr_errors.english: The gloss is uncertain; "auh" is a common Nahuatl conjunction meaning "and."
tr_errors.problem: the gloss is a place name cut off at the gutter; offering the conjunction "auh" invites a false reading

other.note: A blank verso is given a full apparatus of glyph descriptions, glosses, a summary and keywords, as if it carried content. It is a translation of a blank as if it were prose.
The summary and keywords ("Tepeyacac, Ocuilan, Tecalco, Miquiyetlan, conquered towns") are derived from the neighbouring leaf's content and attached to a blank page.

book_verdict: This record's leaf is a blank verso ("7", "11/2"), but its OCR and English transcribe and annotate the strip of the facing leaf at the edge of the frame, so the reader is shown a list of towns that is not on this page. The notes add speculation about the previous page and describe the glyphs wrongly.
